subject.title: RFC 0024: Localization Runtime and Product Coverage

question: Should OpenClaw adopt RFC 0024’s shared localization contracts and sponsor its linked implementation program, or narrow/defer the proposal before implementation proceeds?
rationale: The RFC intentionally introduces new product-wide policies covering locale precedence, Gateway wire metadata, channel safety copy, plugin and command presentation metadata, release claims, and linguistic-review governance; source review cannot safely choose those policies without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded v1
options.body: Approve the compatibility-preserving kernel and name decision owners for Gateway inventory, recipient-locale policy, safety-copy attestation, and language-review governance.

options.title: Narrow the RFC
options.body: Retain the current proposal but defer selected surfaces or contracts until their owners and compatibility requirements are clearer.

options.title: Defer product direction
options.body: Keep this RFC as a draft until a product owner can set durable localization scope and ownership.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a bounded v1
recommendation.body: Approve the compatibility-preserving kernel and name decision owners for Gateway inventory, recipient-locale policy, safety-copy attestation, and language-review governance.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the active RFC coordinator and can incorporate a sponsor’s scope decision, though final product approval belongs to an OpenClaw decision-maker.
